title: Nebulized MSC-Exos for Anti-MDA5+ RP-ILD: Safety and Efficacy Trial
off: Safety and Efficacy Study of Nebulized Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes (MSC-exos) for the Treatment of Anti-MDA5 Positive Dermatomyositis-Associated Rapidly Progressive Interstitial Lung Disease (RP-ILD)
summary:
Objective: To assess the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of nebulized MSC-exos-P1 in patients with anti-MDA5 positive dermatomyositis-associated rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD).

Design: Prospective interventional trial with 10 eligible patients aged 18-75, meeting criteria for RP-ILD and anti-MDA5 positivity. Primary endpoint is safety and tolerability, measured by adverse events within 30 days post-treatment. Secondary endpoints are clinical improvements on days 14 and 28, including serological indicators and chest HRCT scores.

Exclusions: Pregnant/breastfeeding individuals, severe allergies, active pulmonary infections, pulmonary embolism, extracorporeal support treatments, and other specified conditions.

Treatment: Nebulized MSC-exos-P1 daily for 14 days, plus standard care of corticosteroids and immunosuppressants.

Monitoring: Regular vital signs, oxygenation index, and pulmonary function tests. Follow-ups at multiple points up to 12 months.
desc:
This single-center, prospective interventional trial aims to evaluate the safety profile and potential efficacy of nebulized mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-exos-P1) in anti-MDA5 positive dermatomyositis patients with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease. Anti-MDA5 positive RP-ILD represents a critical clinical challenge with mortality rates exceeding 50% despite aggressive immunosuppressive therapy, highlighting the urgent need for novel treatment approaches.

The trial will enroll 10 eligible patients who will receive a 14-day course of daily nebulized MSC-exos-P1 while continuing standard immunosuppressive therapy. Safety monitoring will include daily vital signs, laboratory tests, and adverse event documentation during the treatment period. Efficacy assessments will measure changes in oxygenation parameters, pulmonary function, inflammatory biomarkers, and CT imaging findings at days 14 and 28 compared to baseline.

The scientific rationale for this intervention is based on preclinical evidence demonstrating the immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic properties of MSC-derived exosomes. These nanoparticles have shown the ability to modify alveolar macrophage phenotypes, reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and suppress fibroblast activation - mechanisms that may directly target the pathophysiological processes driving RP-ILD in this patient population. The nebulized delivery system enables direct targeting of affected lung tissue while minimizing systemic exposure.

arms.l: Nebulized MSC-exos for Anti-MDA5+ RP-ILD Treatment
arms.d: This arm of the study involves the administration of nebulized Mesenchymal Stem Cell-derived Exosomes (MSC-exos-P1) as an intervention for patients diagnosed with Anti-MDA5 Positive Dermatomyositis-Associated Rapidly Progressive Interstitial Lung Disease (RP-ILD).

primary.m: Three-Month Mortality Rate and Safety of Nebulized MSC-exos P1

x.titre: Exosomes de cellules souches mésenchymateuses nébulisés dans la PID rapidement progressive anti-MDA5
x.question: Des exosomes dérivés de cellules souches mésenchymateuses, inhalés en nébulisation, sont-ils sûrs et efficaces dans la PID rapidement progressive de la dermatomyosite anti-MDA5 ?
x.contexte:
La dermatomyosite à anticorps anti-MDA5 se complique souvent d'une pneumopathie interstitielle diffuse rapidement progressive (PID-RP). Sa mortalité dépasse 50 % malgré une immunosuppression intensive (corticoïdes, inhibiteurs de la calcineurine, cyclophosphamide, JAK inhibiteurs). Il existe un besoin urgent de nouvelles options.

Les exosomes de cellules souches mésenchymateuses (MSC-exos) ont, en préclinique, des effets immunomodulateurs, anti-inflammatoires et antifibrosants : modification du phénotype des macrophages alvéolaires, baisse des cytokines pro-inflammatoires, freinage de l'activation des fibroblastes. La nébulisation cible directement le poumon et limite l'exposition systémique. Cet essai monocentrique de phase 1 chinois, à bras unique, ajoute MSC-exos-P1 nébulisés au traitement standard pendant 14 jours chez 10 patients.
x.interet: L'étude évalue d'abord la sécurité d'une approche inhalée originale, dans une situation à très forte mortalité. Elle fournira des données préliminaires d'efficacité (oxygénation, scanner, biomarqueurs) pour des essais ultérieurs.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 75 ans atteints de dermatomyosite anti-MDA5 positive avec PID rapidement progressive.
inclusion: Dermatomyosite anti-MDA5 positive selon le consensus chinois 2023
Lésions pulmonaires répondant aux critères de PID rapidement progressive
exclusion: Grossesse, allaitement ou projet de grossesse
Allergie sévère ou allergie au principe actif
Infection pulmonaire sévère, pneumothorax ou épanchement pleural abondant
Ventilation invasive ou assistance extracorporelle (ECMO, plasmaphérèse, etc.)
Insuffisance cardiaque, hépatique ou rénale sévère
Transplantation pulmonaire prévue, cancer du poumon ou nodule suspect
Déficit immunitaire primitif, infection active (VIH, tuberculose)

bras.traitement: MSC-exos-P1 nébulisés quotidiennement pendant 14 jours, en plus des corticoïdes et immunosuppresseurs

x.critere: Mortalité à 3 mois et tolérance du traitement (événements indésirables sous 30 jours).
